title: Israel's security cabinet approves a plan to prepare to take control of Gaza City
body:
Israel's security cabinet approved a plan to prepare to take control of Gaza City late on Thursday 7 August 2025, according to a statement from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office reported on 8 August. Israel did not say when the takeover would begin. Local media reported that it would not be immediate and that residents would first be ordered to evacuate.

Netanyahu's office said the statement set out several key principles: dismantling Hamas's arsenal, securing the return of all hostages living or dead, demilitarizing the Gaza Strip, keeping Israeli security control over the territory, and creating an alternative civilian administration that is neither Hamas nor the Palestinian Authority. The military was also to ensure that humanitarian aid reached civilians outside combat zones. Netanyahu said a detailed plan would be drawn up for the post-Hamas administration and that the Palestinian Authority would be excluded. In an interview he said: "We don't want to keep it. We want to have a security perimeter, but we don't want to govern it."

Citing the BBC, the report said officials considered the move likely to be the first phase of a full takeover that could take months. Citing the Times of Israel, it said Egypt had warned the United States that the plan could prompt Hamas to kill Israeli hostages, and that Hamas and allied groups reportedly had orders to neutralize captives if their positions were besieged and escape became impossible. Hamas had not issued a public response to the cabinet decision.
